findings.paper_title: 07(1 of 2) GAC 7th Oct Q1 Risk OPEN V.1
findings.headline: Two strategic issues were closed during Q1 2026-27: Cwmbwrla Flooding (resolved May 2026) and Net Zero 2030 Target (closed June 2026).
findings.detail: Cwmbwrla Flooding was scored 16 (Red) in Q4 and resolved when the flood risk was reduced, blockage removed, and the road reopened. Net Zero 2030 Target was scored 12 (Red) in Q4 and closed when the council's agenda expanded to adaptation and decarbonisation.
findings.matters: Closure of previously Red-rated issues demonstrates that governance action and management focus can reduce exposure where controls are clearly owned and actively monitored.
findings.figures: 2 issues closed; Cwmbwrla Flooding previously Red score 16; Net Zero 2030 Target previously Red score 12
findings.quote: Cwmbwrla Flooding, which was scored 16 (Red) in Q4, was resolved in May as the flood risk was reduced, blockage removed, and Heol y Gors reopened. Net Zero 2030 Target, which scored 12 (Red) in Q4, was closed in June to reflect the widening of the agenda to adaptation and decarbonisation.

findings.paper_title: 07(1 of 2) GAC 7th Oct Q1 Risk OPEN V.1
findings.headline: Four new strategic risks were added in Q1, indicating increasing exposure to statutory, governance, compliance, community safety and operational resilience pressures.
findings.detail: While individual details are excluded from the public version due to commercial, legal or security sensitivity, the new risks collectively signal emerging regulatory, governance or operational challenges. The paper notes these may require coordinated action across directorates.
findings.matters: New risks in statutory, governance and compliance areas may indicate emerging regulatory or operational challenges that could affect the council's ability to meet statutory duties or require remedial investment.
findings.figures: 4 new strategic risks added in Q1 2026-27
findings.quote: the new risks indicate increasing exposure to statutory, governance, compliance, community safety and operational resilience pressures, which may require coordinated action across directorates.

findings.paper_title: 07(1 of 2) GAC 7th Oct Q1 Risk OPEN V.1
findings.headline: Three strategic issues remain open and rated Red: pressure on temporary accommodation availability, homelessness and housing supply, and Disabled Facilities Grants demand and delivery.
findings.detail: These three issues scored statically between Q4 and Q1, with no improvement. The paper notes these are complex issues requiring sustained intervention over a longer period. All three have direct financial implications for council spending on housing support and vulnerable people.
findings.matters: Static Red-rated issues on housing and accommodation indicate unresolved demand pressures that require continued council spending and constrain financial flexibility.
findings.figures: 3 strategic issues; all rated Red; all static between Q4 and Q1
findings.quote: During Quarter 1, three Strategic Issues were reported: Pressure on the availability of temporary accommodation; Homelessness and Housing Supply; and Disabled Facilities Grants – demand, programme delivery and budget performance. All three were reviewed and rated Red.

findings.paper_title: 07(1 of 2) GAC 7th Oct Q1 Risk OPEN V.1
findings.headline: Financial Control – MTFP Delivery risk remains at residual score 20, down from 25 in Q4 but still the second-highest risk, reflecting ongoing inflation and savings delivery pressures.
findings.detail: While this risk has reduced by 5 points, the score of 20 indicates significant continued exposure. The paper attributes it to persistent challenges in delivering the medium-term financial plan against inflation and required savings.
findings.matters: A residual score of 20 on MTFP delivery indicates sustained pressure on the council's ability to deliver its medium-term financial strategy, with implications for budget sustainability beyond 2026-27.
findings.figures: Financial Control – MTFP Delivery residual score 20 (Q1 2026-27); down from 25 (Q4 2025-26)
findings.quote: Financial Control – MTFP Delivery 20 Remains high at 20, reflecting ongoing MTFP delivery, inflation and savings pressures. Reduced from 25 but still requires close oversight.

findings.paper_title: 07(1 of 2) GAC 7th Oct Q1 Risk OPEN V.1
findings.headline: Red strategic risks increased from 13 to 18, now representing 55% of the council's 33 strategic risks.
findings.detail: The council reported 33 strategic risks in Q1, with 18 rated Red and 15 Amber. This represents both an increase in absolute number and proportion of high-severity risks. The paper attributes the shift mainly to financial resilience and supply chain volatility pressures.
findings.matters: An increase in high-severity risks indicates the council is managing a more complex and constrained operating environment that could affect service delivery and financial stability.
findings.figures: Red strategic risks: 13 (Q4 2025-26) to 18 (Q1 2026-27); total strategic risks 33 (18 Red 55%, 15 Amber 45%)
findings.quote: During Quarter 1, 33 Strategic Risks were reported, 18 were rated Red (55%) and 15 rated Amber (45%).

findings.paper_title: 07(1 of 2) GAC 7th Oct Q1 Risk OPEN V.1
findings.headline: Living Within Budget risk residual score increased from 8 to 25, the maximum score, driven by outturn, unfunded pressures, pay and inflation.
findings.detail: This is now the council's highest-scoring strategic risk. The jump from 8 to 25 in a single quarter represents a material deterioration in the council's ability to remain within its annual budget, driven by specific and immediate cost pressures rather than medium-term structural issues.
findings.matters: A risk at maximum residual score on the annual budget indicates the council faces material and immediate financial pressure that threatens the delivery of the 2026-27 financial plan.
findings.figures: Residual score increased from 8 to 25; score of 25 is the maximum
findings.quote: Increased from 8 to 25, driven by outturn, unfunded pressures, pay and inflation. This is the key financial resilience risk for Q1.

findings.paper_title: 04 (1 of 1) - GAC report Management of absence and agency workers
findings.headline: Council identifies sickness absence and its indirect financial impact as material ongoing workforce risk requiring sustained management attention
findings.detail: The council states in its conclusion that despite progress and improvements implemented, sickness absence and its indirect financial impact continue to represent a material workforce risk requiring sustained management attention. The council will continue monitoring effectiveness through monthly performance data, quarterly reporting, and staff and manager feedback.
findings.matters: A council's own identification of unresolved material risk in a cost-driving area indicates the problem has not been fully resolved and cost pressures may continue despite current quarterly improvements.
findings.figures: None
findings.quote: Notwithstanding this progress, sickness absence and its indirect financial impact continue to represent a material workforce risk that requires sustained management attention

findings.paper_title: 04 (1 of 1) - GAC report Management of absence and agency workers
findings.headline: Sickness absence performance at 3.92 days per FTE remains 1.42 days above quarterly target of 2.5 days
findings.detail: Despite the 14.6% improvement, the council continues to miss its absence target. Quarter 1 performance was 3.92 days per FTE against a target trajectory of 2.5 days per FTE. The report notes sickness absence levels in some service areas, particularly operational and frontline services where national and sector-wide pressures remain significant, continue to exceed corporate targets.
findings.matters: Failure to meet absence targets indicates unresolved service-level pressures that risk continued agency spending, operational delivery challenges, and sustained demand for support services.
findings.figures: 3.92 days per FTE actual vs 2.5 days per FTE target; 1.42 days per FTE above target
findings.quote: The Quarter 1 position equates to approximately 3.92 days lost per FTE, against the authority's quarterly target trajectory of 2.5 days per FTE. Performance therefore remains around 1.42 days per FTE above target.

findings.paper_title: 04 (1 of 1) - GAC report Management of absence and agency workers
findings.headline: Agency expenditure fell 10.2% year-on-year to £1.636 million in Quarter 1 2026
findings.detail: Agency spend reduced from £1.822 million in Q1 2025 to £1.636 million in Q1 2026, representing a £186,000 reduction. The improvement was mainly driven by Place directorate (£322,600 reduction) and Education (£43,000 reduction), though partly offset by increases in Corporate Services (£97,100) and Finance (£71,100). ALS Managed Services spend fell 28.3% to £772,000.
findings.matters: Agency spending is a controllable cost that directly impacts council budgets and financial resilience; a £186,000 quarterly reduction could represent approximately £744,000 in annual savings if sustained.
findings.figures: £1.822m Q1 2025 → £1.636m Q1 2026; £186,000 (10.2%) reduction; Place -£322,600; Education -£43,000; Corporate Services +£97,100; Finance +£71,100; ALS Managed Services -£305,000 (28.3% to £772,000)
findings.quote: Agency spend reduced from £1.822 million in Quarter 1 (April to June) 2025/26 to £1.636 million in Quarter 1 2026/27. This represents a year-on-year reduction of approximately £186,000, or 10.2%.

findings.paper_title: 04 (1 of 1) - GAC report Management of absence and agency workers
findings.headline: Sickness absence fell 14.6% year-on-year to 35,657.5 days in Quarter 1 2026
findings.detail: Working days lost reduced from 41,771 days in Q1 2025 to 35,657.5 days in Q1 2026. Improvements recorded across five of six reporting areas, with Schools (21.6% reduction), Education (19.2%), and Corporate Services (27.3%) showing the largest proportionate reductions.
findings.matters: Sickness absence drives both operational disruption and agency spending; a 14.6% reduction indicates improved workforce health and cost control, reducing reliance on temporary staffing.
findings.figures: 41,771 days Q1 2025 → 35,657.5 days Q1 2026; 14.6% reduction; Schools -2,554 days (21.6%); Social Services -1,436 days (12.7%); Education -966.5 days (19.2%); Corporate Services -282.5 days (27.3%)
findings.quote: Total working days lost reduced from 41,771 days in Quarter 1 2025 to 35,657.5 days in Quarter 1 2026, a reduction of 6,113.5 days, or 14.6%.

findings.paper_title: 05 (1 of 3) - Housing reponse to Audit Wales Report on Temporary accommodation
findings.headline: Audit Wales 2025 report identified rising costs and demand pressures in temporary accommodation across Wales, with councils focusing too narrowly on short-term cost control.
findings.detail: A 2025 Audit Wales review found temporary accommodation a growing pressure across Welsh councils, with councils viewing value for money too narrowly. There was focus on short-term cost control rather than outcomes, prevention, and whole-system performance. This prompted Audit Wales to examine Swansea's specific arrangements in June 2026.
findings.matters: Provides context that Swansea's temporary accommodation pressures and redesign approach are relevant to other finance directors facing similar sector-wide challenges.
findings.figures: None in this paper
findings.quote: In 2025, a report from Audit Wales Temporary accommodation, long-term crisis? highlighted rising cost and demand pressures across Wales. It found that councils often view value for money too narrowly. There is more focus on short-term cost control rather than outcomes, prevention, and whole system performance.

findings.paper_title: 05 (1 of 3) - Housing reponse to Audit Wales Report on Temporary accommodation
findings.headline: Audit Wales found council's arrangements to monitor value for money in temporary accommodation are not yet fully developed.
findings.detail: Audit Wales concluded that while the council understands demand well and has redesigned its approach, arrangements to monitor overall value for money require development. The council intends to develop wider person-centred outcome measures and a comprehensive framework covering financial, service, and outcomes data to assess whether the redesign delivers value for money.
findings.matters: Lenders and finance directors need assurance that service redesigns are being monitored against outcomes and value for money, not just cost control.
findings.figures: One audit recommendation
findings.quote: The report also concluded that the Council's arrangements to monitor the overall value for money of its new approach are not yet fully developed.

findings.paper_title: 05 (1 of 3) - Housing reponse to Audit Wales Report on Temporary accommodation
findings.headline: Council opening two new temporary accommodation facilities, with Llys Glas opened January 2026 and second facility opening January/February 2027.
findings.detail: The council is in early stages of delivering a new approach to temporary accommodation through capital investment. Llys Glas opened on schedule in January 2026, and a second large-scale temporary supported housing project is scheduled to open January/February 2027. This responds to rising cost and demand pressures in temporary accommodation identified across Wales.
findings.matters: Finance directors and lenders track how councils invest capital to manage growing service pressures; temporary accommodation is identified as a sector-wide issue.
findings.figures: Llys Glas opened January 2026; second facility January/February 2027
findings.quote: The Council is in the early stages of delivering its new approach which includes the development of two temporary accommodation facilities. Llys Glas opened in January 2026, and the 2nd large-scale temporary supported housing project will be opened in January/February 2027.

findings.paper_title: 09 (2 of 2) - Appendix 1 - Fraud Function Annual Plan 2026-27
findings.headline: Council tax discount verification contract with DataTank ended 31 March 2026; replacement system not yet specified
findings.detail: The council had commissioned DataTank in 2023 to identify improper Single Person Discount awards and carry out rolling review instead of bi-annual checks. That contract has now ended. The Revenues section is 'considering other options that will be more cost effective and provide enhanced results', but no specific replacement system is named in this plan.
findings.matters: Single Person Discounts are identified by CIPFA as high-fraud-risk area; the change in verification method creates a transition period during which the robustness of fraud detection may be unclear.
findings.figures: Contract ended 31 March 2026
findings.quote: In 2023 'Data Tank' was commissioned to identify cases where an award of SPD may not be appropriate and review every match on a rolling review rather than a bi-annual review. The contract with Datatank has now ended 31st March 2026, and the Revenues section are considering other options that will be more cost effective and provide enhanced results

findings.paper_title: 09 (2 of 2) - Appendix 1 - Fraud Function Annual Plan 2026-27
findings.headline: Fraud Function staffed by three officers; expansion of proactive work contingent on additional resources not yet secured
findings.detail: The council's fraud investigation team consists of three qualified full-time investigators, with other audit staff assisting as needed. The plan acknowledges that proactive fraud activity depends on planned resource expansion. The council states that 'the caseload will continue to be monitored' and the Section 151 Officer and Audit Committee will consider additional resources 'notwithstanding the overall resource constraints'.
findings.matters: A council's fraud detection capability is directly constrained by investigation capacity; resource limitations may limit ability to identify fraud proactively in high-risk areas.
findings.figures: 3 qualified full-time investigators
findings.quote: An Audit based Fraud Function consists of 3 officers, but existing Audit staff can assist Fraud Function staff as and when appropriate. The caseload will continue to be monitored and if necessary, notwithstanding the overall resource constraints, the Section 151 Officer and Audit Committee will continue to give due regard to whether additional resource needs to be applied to the fraud function.

findings.paper_title: 06 (1 of 3) - GAC report Recruitment and Retention report
findings.headline: Council accepted both audit recommendations; management response plan established with six-month progress checkpoint
findings.detail: Council accepted both recommendations in full and established a management response with identified responsible officers and target completion dates. The Workforce OD Transformation Board will oversee delivery with progress monitored through existing governance structures. A further progress report to the Governance & Audit Committee is scheduled for six months.
findings.matters: Shows council's accountability structure and reporting timeline for remediation of audit findings
findings.figures: 6-month reporting cycle
findings.quote: A further progress report will be provided to the Governance and Audit Committee in six months to enable Members to review implementation progress and the impact of the actions taken

findings.paper_title: 06 (1 of 3) - GAC report Recruitment and Retention report
findings.headline: Council lacks sufficient evaluation of whether recruitment spending is delivering value for money and effectiveness
findings.detail: Audit review identified that resources are being invested in recruitment and retention initiatives but without sufficient evidence of their effectiveness or value for money. This represents a control gap where spending is proceeding without adequate evaluation of impact or outcomes.
findings.matters: Finance directors require assurance that spending is achieving intended outcomes; evaluation gaps create risk of ineffective or wasteful investment
findings.figures: N/A
findings.quote: resources continue to be invested in recruitment and retention initiatives without sufficient evidence of effectiveness, impact or value for money

findings.paper_title: 06 (1 of 3) - GAC report Recruitment and Retention report
findings.headline: Audit identified risk that unidentified recruitment challenges could increase agency staffing costs and affect service resilience
findings.detail: Audit Wales flagged that if recruitment and retention challenges are not identified early enough, the council could face increased reliance on costly agency or temporary staffing arrangements and service resilience impacts. This risk is material because uncontrolled agency staffing growth typically drives significant budget pressure.
findings.matters: Finance officers monitor workforce cost trends; uncontrolled agency staffing increases budget pressure and reduces council's capacity to deliver services
findings.figures: N/A
findings.quote: This could affect workforce sustainability, increase reliance on agency or temporary staffing arrangements and impact service resilience
